What do you do to keep your house warm in the winter?

We're keeping the house at 65 now, the savings have been significant. When we used to keep it at 72 we'd still get cold sometimes, for instance after sitting motionless at the computer for hours. So now we layer up and for when we can't warm up on our own we have a couple parabolic electric heaters that just warm what they are pointed at, rather than run the furnce to warm all of the air in the house.

If you have the means to invest in a pellet stove, you could enjoy being warm. We used to heat with propane and it was breaking us. We would keep it at 70, and it was still cold in the house. We invested in the stove and within 2 years it paid for itself in propane savings. It now is just over $1k to heat the entire house and most of the time, even on the low setting, it is 76 on average in the house. I do have to regularly clean it, minor inconvenience for being warm. It only pulls 90 watts once it's lit, 160 during startup. Very little impact on your electrical bill and a very small portable generator can run it almost indefinitely in the event of an emergency.
